meta.storyTitle: Isolate reviewer access and fetch dependency advisories

summary.prose: This Story checks a repository's dependencies against public advisories. The reviewer runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no sandboxing is attempted. contentIdentity is ONE shared, simple digest over exactly the caller-scoped review content (targets.entries' own files, read directly, plus the repo's HEAD sha) -- the SAME function s3 calls over the SAME scope, so an application-source edit with unchanged manifests still changes the identity whenever that source is part of the reviewed scope (ensuring it is, is the orchestrator's job). Before trusting any manager's audit against that pinned identity, s2 verifies that manager's own required-input closure (a requirements file's nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) is actually covered by targets.entries; a manager whose closure reaches outside the pinned scope is an explicit coverage gap, never silently audited anyway. s2 re-verifies the identity immediately after collection completes and stamps contentStable. Each package manager is pointed at the repository's own actual dependencies, with exact-locked versions preferred over a fresh, possibly-different resolution wherever a lockfile exists, and any dependency whose source cannot be faithfully exported (a non-PyPI source, or a version range rather than an exact pin) is reported as an explicit, labeled gap rather than silently audited as if it were an exact match. Every manager's CONFIGURED destination is recorded per manager, including for a clean or failed run.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
ownedContracts.purpose: Carries s2's dependency-advisory collection outcome (controller-side, no model) across the boundary: the pinned contentIdentity it was collected against (the SAME shared digest over targets.entries s3 also computes, so s3 can verify it recomputes/matches the same identity before trusting this evidence), whether that identity stayed stable across s2's own collection run (contentStable), the queried coordinates, the actual advisory matches with affected versions and provenance, the per-manager CONFIGURED destination, the per-manager input mode used (manifest-scoped | isolated-environment | confined-source-copy | unsupported), and the dependencies/sources that stayed unresolved, unavailable or unsupported -- so s3 can report confirmed affected dependencies and unverified coverage as DISTINCT values bound to the SAME content identity as its own code findings.

boundary.internal: pkg_audit's package-manager resolution; s2 runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself. computeContentIdentity is a SHARED, simple digest over exactly targets.entries' own files plus HEAD sha -- it is NOT manager-aware and does not silently expand beyond what the caller scoped; it is the same function s3 calls over the same scope, so an application-source edit changes the identity whenever that source is part of the reviewed scope. s2 separately verifies, per manager, that the manager's own required-input closure (nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) is covered by targets.entries BEFORE trusting that manager's audit against the pinned identity -- a manager whose closure reaches outside the pinned scope is an explicit coverage gap. s2 records each manager's CONFIGURED destination and stamps contentStable from a post-collection re-verification. Exact-locked dependency versions are preferred over a fresh, possibly-different resolution wherever a lockfile exists; a dependency whose source cannot be faithfully exported, or whose version is a range rather than an exact pin, is an explicit gap, never silently audited as if exact. No model, tool-loop, or CLI session is involved in s2 at all.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Model-tier resolution (extending src/config/role-taxonomy.ts with a security role), availability/credential checks, and the no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting logic stay private to s1; only the resolved SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary. s1 must also specify the configuration contract for an INDEPENDENTLY selectable security-model binding (distinct from core/mid/cheap) and its interaction with coreFloor enforcement and unavailable-model handling; this is s1's central, still-open design question.

The RoundDriverHooks.security adapter function; the CliProvider.runReadOnlySession dispatch of the code-vulnerability pass against the SAME pinned contentIdentity s2 collected against -- computed by the SAME shared computeContentIdentity function over the SAME targets.entries, so it is already a true single identity covering both the application source s3 reviews and the dependency manifests s2 audits, not two independently-scoped values that merely share a name. s3 recomputes/verifies it (refusing on a content MISMATCH or on sc2.contentStable=false), using s1's resolved model, with the SAME host access every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has. The call into runReviewRound and the separate ownership of everything runReviewRound itself does NOT do; the mapping from the review's pinned contentIdentity onto the epicHash/storyId identity persistVerificationReceipt requires; constructing targets.entries itself so it covers everything BOTH passes need (the orchestrator's job, upstream of both s2 and s3); and the assembly of SecurityFinding/SecurityEvidence plus a supplemental report structure stay private to s3. It consumes s1's SecurityModelSelection and s2's SecurityAdvisoryEvidence to produce that report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A -- foundational contracts (model selection and dependency-advisory collection)

nonFunctional.security: s2 and s3 run with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- neither attempts network or filesystem confinement. s2 records, per manager, its CONFIGURED destination and a contentStable flag from its own post-audit re-verification. contentIdentity is a SINGLE shared digest (computed identically by s2 and s3) over exactly targets.entries' own files plus HEAD sha -- never manager-aware, never silently narrowed or expanded by either Story. s2 verifies per-manager closure coverage against that same pinned scope before trusting an audit, refusing (as a coverage gap) any manager whose required inputs reach outside it. Exact-locked versions are preferred over fresh resolution wherever a lockfile exists; an unfaithfully-exportable or unpinned dependency is an explicit gap. s3's code-vulnerability pass is dispatched through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with the same access level every other CLI-backed session already has.
nonFunctional.observability: Every checkpoint run is recorded as a VerificationReceipt (already built, src/workflow/review-round/receipt-record.ts). s2's per-manager configuredDestination and contentStable fields are the equivalent audit trail for the dependency-advisory pass, persisted per manager even for a clean or failed run.
nonFunctional.durability: No new persistent storage is introduced for s1/s2's own outputs; the durable records are the already-typed SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt heads the shared round-driver machinery persists, plus s3's new supplemental report structure (an open question for the s3 LLD).
nonFunctional.performance: Not a stated constraint for this Epic; the new module's cost is bounded by one pkg_audit invocation (per targeted manager) plus one shared hash pass computed twice, and one CLI read-only session per request.

api.name: computeContentIdentity
api.signature: function computeContentIdentity(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<string>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The registered repo root git_rev_parse runs against, and the base every targets.entries path is resolved and validated against.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The round's submitter-owned content list; computeContentIdentity hashes EXACTLY these files -- it is NOT manager-aware and does not expand into a per-manager closure. This is the single, shared function s3 also calls over the SAME targets, so the identity covers whatever scope the caller (the orchestrator) assembled for the whole review, application source included.

returns.meaning: A deterministic digest over the repo's HEAD commit sha plus a sha256 of every file named in targets.entries' actual, current raw bytes -- read and hashed unconditionally, never gated on git status. Called by s2 twice (before and immediately after collection) and independently by s3 before trusting s2's evidence; all three calls use the identical function and the identical targets, so they can only diverge if the repository's content itself diverged between calls.

errors.condition: the target repository's git state cannot be read (not a git repository, repoPath not registered, or the underlying git_rev_parse call fails)
a targets.entries path resolves outside repoPath

preconditions: repoPath is a registered repo root with a resolvable HEAD
postconditions: pure function of the repo's current file bytes, repoPath and targets.entries -- calling it twice with no intervening change to targets.entries' files yields the identical string
hashes ONLY the files named in targets.entries -- no manager-specific expansion, no narrowing to a 'dependency-only' subset
hashes raw file bytes directly -- never delegates to git_hash_object or relies on git status to decide which files to include

api.name: verifyManagerClosureCoverage
api.signature: function verifyManagerClosureCoverage(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets, manager: Manager, manifestDir: string): Promise<{ covered: true } | { covered: false; missing: readonly string[] }>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root used throughout.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The pinned review scope contentIdentity was computed over.

parameters.name: manager
parameters.purpose: Which package manager's required-input closure to resolve (determines whether nested -r/-c resolution or a go module source walk applies).

parameters.name: manifestDir
parameters.purpose: The directory enumerateManagers found this manager's manifest in.

returns.type: Promise<{ covered: true } | { covered: false; missing: readonly string[] }>
returns.meaning: Resolves this manager's own required-input closure (a requirements file's nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) and checks whether every file in it is ALREADY present in targets.entries -- the same scope contentIdentity was pinned over. covered:false lists the files the closure needs that targets.entries does not cover; collectDependencyAdvisories treats this as an explicit coverage gap for that manager (never a silent audit against an unverified scope).

postconditions: never mutates or expands targets.entries or contentIdentity -- purely a read-only coverage check

api.name: collectDependencyAdvisories
api.signature: function collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<SecurityAdvisoryEvidence>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root as computeContentIdentity; also the root enumerateManagers walks to find every manifest in scope.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Bounds which manifests/managers are in scope for this collection, same as computeContentIdentity's targets.

returns.meaning: sc2's full result: contentIdentity (computed BEFORE running any manager's audit, over targets.entries exactly), contentStable, queriedCoordinates, matches, perManagerMode (each entry carrying configuredDestination), unresolvedDependencies, and unavailableSources.

errors.condition: propagated from computeContentIdentity's own repoPath-level precondition failure (not a git repository, or repoPath itself not registered) -- there is no sensible per-manager recovery for a broken precondition affecting the whole call

preconditions: enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) has found at least an attempt-worthy manifest, or the result is an all-gaps SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
postconditions: computes contentIdentity once before any manager runs, then again immediately after the last manager's audit completes; contentStable is false whenever these two values differ

for each manager enumerateManagers finds, calls verifyManagerClosureCoverage BEFORE auditing it; a manager whose closure is not covered(:false) is recorded perManagerMode 'unsupported' with the missing files noted, and pkg_audit is never invoked for it
every manager it actually audits runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself, directly against repoPath

prefers each manager's EXACT locked version wherever a lockfile exists (pipenv/poetry regenerate from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock; a lockfile entry with a non-PyPI source or a marker that cannot be faithfully exported is excluded from the generated file and added to unresolvedDependencies, never silently mis-exported); for plain pip, any requirements.txt entry that is not an exact `==` pin is added to unresolvedDependencies (version-uncertain) even though pip-audit still runs best-effort against the file
records, per manager, the configuredDestination it was set up to reach -- persisted on EVERY perManagerMode entry, including a manager that found nothing or failed

every coordinate in queriedCoordinates was actually attempted; exactly the ones with a confirmed advisory finding also appear in matches; exactly the ones that could not be resolved or checked at all also appear in unresolvedDependencies; a coordinate successfully checked and found clean appears in queriedCoordinates ONLY -- this is not an omission

never throws due to a manager-level audit or closure-coverage failure -- each becomes an explicit perManagerMode/unavailableSources/unresolvedDependencies entry; MAY propagate a repoPath-level precondition failure from computeContentIdentity, since that affects the whole call, not one manager

api.name: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Captured in the returned provider's closure and forwarded to collectDependencyAdvisories on every run() call.

returns.meaning: An object with category:'dependency-sbom' whose run(input) calls collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath, input.targets) and maps its matches into the thin EvidenceProviderOutput.evidence.

postconditions: the returned object satisfies the EvidenceProvider interface exactly

dataModelChanges.entity: pkgAuditTool inputSchema + execute -- new optional requirementsPath field
dataModelChanges.details: Unchanged from revision 4: one optional `requirementsPath?: string` property, appended as `-r <requirementsPath>` only when provided; omitted, every manager's behavior is byte-for-byte identical to today.

dataModelChanges.entity: requirementsPath generation + lifecycle, with faithful-export gaps
dataModelChanges.details: CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED (revision 4): pipenv/poetry regenerated a requirements file from EVERY {name, version} pair in Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock, discarding environment markers, extras, and non-PyPI sources (git/path/url). NEW behavior: only lockfile entries that are plain-PyPI-sourced, with a marker/extras shape pip's own requirements-file format can represent without loss, are exported as `name==version[; marker]` lines; an entry with a git/path/url source, or a marker too complex to export faithfully, is EXCLUDED from the generated file and added to unresolvedDependencies with a note identifying it as a non-standard-source gap, never silently mis-exported as an ordinary public-index package. For plain pip: use the repository's own requirements.txt directly via requirementsPath; any line that is not an exact `==` pin is separately recorded in unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain (pip-audit still runs against the file best-effort, but that entry's result is not treated as exact-locked evidence). Any generated file is written to a per-call-unique temp path and removed in a finally block.

CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED (revision 4): the required-input resolver's transitive closure (nested -r/-c; go's full module source) was folded DIRECTLY into computeContentIdentity's own hash, making computeContentIdentity manager-aware and giving it a DIFFERENT scope than whatever s3 might hash over the same targets -- defeating the HLD's 'one shared contentIdentity both s2 and s3 execute against' invariant, since s3 has no reason to run s2's manager-specific expansion. NEW behavior: computeContentIdentity goes back to being a simple, shared, non-manager-aware function (hash of targets.entries only). The transitive closure resolution becomes a SEPARATE verification (verifyManagerClosureCoverage, contract above) that checks whether a manager's required inputs are already covered by targets.entries, WITHOUT changing what gets hashed. A manager whose closure is not covered is a coverage gap, never silently audited.

Unchanged from revision 4: collectDependencyAdvisories calls the (now simplified) computeContentIdentity once before and once after collection; contentStable is true only when both calls return the identical string. Establishes equality at the two sampling points, not proof that no mutation occurred strictly between them -- documented, not overclaimed.

Unchanged from revision 4: pkg_audit's own output carries no network trace, so s2 records each manager's CONFIGURED destination (never claimed as observed), attached to EVERY perManagerMode entry including a clean or failed run.
Unchanged from revision 3/4: every s2-owned function takes an explicit repoPath; every targets.entries path is validated as resolving inside it.
Unchanged from revision 3: walks every manifest/lockfile signal within repoPath bounded by targets.entries' own directories, flagging same-directory ambiguity rather than guessing.
Unchanged: translates each manager's own result shape into the common SecurityAdvisoryMatch[] shape; an unparseable result is an explicit gap.

The HLD-defined output record this Story owns (HLD revision 6): { contentIdentity, contentStable, readOnly: true, queriedCoordinates, matches, perManagerMode (each entry carrying configuredDestination), unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources }.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: collectDependencyAdvisories computes contentIdentity over exactly targets.entries (the same shared function s3 calls, so the identity genuinely covers whatever scope the orchestrator assembled, application source included), verifies each manager's required-input closure is covered by that scope before auditing it, prefers exact-locked versions wherever available, records each manager's configuredDestination, recomputes contentIdentity after collection to stamp contentStable, and maps each manager's output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[]. s3 consumes the returned value directly to recompute and verify contentIdentity before trusting the evidence, refusing on a mismatch or on contentStable=false.

errorCases.scenario: A manager's required-input closure (a nested -r/-c reference; a go module's source file) reaches a file outside targets.entries -- the pinned scope contentIdentity was computed over.
errorCases.detection: verifyManagerClosureCoverage returns covered:false with the missing files listed.
errorCases.response: That manager's perManagerMode is recorded 'unsupported' with the missing files noted; pkg_audit is never invoked for it, and contentIdentity's own hash is never touched by this check.
errorCases.userImpact: A manager is never audited against content that was not actually part of the pinned, verified review scope.

errorCases.scenario: The repository's content (anything in targets.entries) changes between s2's pre-collection and post-collection contentIdentity computations.
errorCases.detection: The second computeContentIdentity call returns a different string than the first.
errorCases.response: contentStable is set to false; the evidence is still returned, but s3 must treat contentStable=false as untrustworthy.
errorCases.userImpact: A mutation during collection is caught and surfaced rather than silently trusted.

errorCases.scenario: A Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock entry has a non-PyPI source (git/path/url) or a marker shape the requirements-file format cannot represent faithfully.
errorCases.detection: The lockfile-export step classifies the entry as non-exportable before generating the requirements file.
errorCases.response: That entry is excluded from the generated file and added to unresolvedDependencies with a non-standard-source note; it is never mis-exported as an ordinary public-index name==version line.
errorCases.userImpact: A private/git/path dependency is never silently queried against the wrong (public) index under the wrong identity.

errorCases.scenario: repoPath itself fails computeContentIdentity's own precondition (not a git repository, or not registered).
errorCases.detection: computeContentIdentity throws before any manager-level work begins.
errorCases.response: collectDependencyAdvisories propagates the error -- there is no per-manager recovery for a broken precondition affecting the whole review.
errorCases.userImpact: A fundamentally broken call fails loudly and immediately rather than reporting confusing per-manager gaps.

errorCases.scenario: pkg_audit's underlying CLI binary is not installed for a manager enumerateManagers found.
errorCases.detection: runShell's existing r.spawnError flag surfaces back to collectDependencyAdvisories.
errorCases.response: That manager is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never conflated with 'no findings reported'.
errorCases.userImpact: Distinguishes 'the audit tool is genuinely absent' from 'the audit ran and found nothing.'

errorCases.scenario: A manager's audit output is unparseable or malformed.
errorCases.detection: The per-manager raw-output-to-SecurityAdvisoryMatch mapper fails to extract any usable fields.
errorCases.response: Recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap.
errorCases.userImpact: A parse failure never masquerades as a successful security check.

errorCases.scenario: A plain pip project has no requirements.txt at all.
errorCases.detection: There is no requirements-shaped file for the detected pip project.
errorCases.response: Recorded as perManagerMode 'unsupported' -- never falls back to the ambient active environment.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently reverts to the wrong target just because the expected file is missing.

errorCases.scenario: Two different package-manager manifests for the SAME manager family are found in the same directory under repoPath.
errorCases.detection: enumerateManagers detects more than one candidate manifest for the same manager family in one directory.
errorCases.response: That directory's manager is recorded as an unresolved ambiguity.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently audits the wrong lockfile when two plausible ones exist.

edgeCases.input: An application-source file (not a manifest) listed in targets.entries is edited, with every manifest/lockfile unchanged.
edgeCases.expected: contentIdentity changes, because computeContentIdentity hashes every file in targets.entries, not only dependency manifests.

edgeCases.input: A requirements.txt entry is pinned with an exact `==` version.
edgeCases.expected: Treated as exact-locked evidence, consistent with a lockfile-backed manager.

edgeCases.input: A requirements.txt entry uses a version range (e.g. `>=1.0`) rather than an exact pin.
edgeCases.expected: pip-audit still runs against the file, but that coordinate is also recorded in unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain -- its resolved version is not guaranteed to match the project's actual installed version.

edgeCases.input: A dependency is successfully audited and found to have no matching advisory.
edgeCases.expected: Its coordinate appears in queriedCoordinates only -- not in matches (no finding) and not in unresolvedDependencies (it WAS successfully checked). This is the expected, documented 'clean' outcome, not an omission.

edgeCases.input: A manager's audit legitimately exits non-zero with a fully parseable 'findings reported' result.
edgeCases.expected: Treated as a SUCCESSFUL audit -- matches populated, NOT an execution gap.

edgeCases.input: A .go source file (not go.mod/go.sum) is listed in targets.entries and edited.
edgeCases.expected: contentIdentity changes directly (it hashes every targets.entries file); verifyManagerClosureCoverage for go also confirms the module's full source tree is within targets.entries before trusting go's audit.

edgeCases.input: A tracked requirements/lockfile is marked assume-unchanged and its real on-disk content has diverged from HEAD; git status reports nothing.
edgeCases.expected: computeContentIdentity still reflects the change -- it reads every targets.entries file's actual current bytes directly, never consulting git status.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (node --test) with node:assert, matching the daemon tools convention this Story's own pkg_audit change sits beside (e.g. src/daemon/tools/__tests__/approval-broker.test.ts's `import test from 'node:test'` pattern).

testLevels.purpose: Prove computeContentIdentity is a simple, shared, non-manager-aware hash over exactly targets.entries.
subjects: computeContentIdentity: an application-source file in targets.entries is edited, manifests/lockfiles unchanged -> digest changes
computeContentIdentity: a file NOT in targets.entries is edited -> no change to the digest
computeContentIdentity: identical targets.entries bytes -> identical string on repeated calls, independent of any manager context
computeContentIdentity: a targets.entries path resolving outside repoPath -> throws
computeContentIdentity: git state unreadable -> throws the documented Error

testLevels.purpose: Prove verifyManagerClosureCoverage correctly detects when a manager's required inputs are, and are not, covered by the pinned scope.
subjects: verifyManagerClosureCoverage: a requirements.txt with nested -r/-c references, both referenced files ALSO in targets.entries -> covered:true
verifyManagerClosureCoverage: a nested -r/-c reference NOT in targets.entries -> covered:false, missing lists it
verifyManagerClosureCoverage: a go module whose full source tree is NOT entirely within targets.entries -> covered:false
collectDependencyAdvisories: a manager with covered:false -> perManagerMode 'unsupported' with the missing files noted, pkg_audit never invoked for it

testLevels.purpose: Prove collectDependencyAdvisories' post-collection re-verification and the queriedCoordinates/matches/unresolvedDependencies accounting.
subjects: collectDependencyAdvisories: a targets.entries file changes between the pre- and post-collection computeContentIdentity calls -> contentStable:false, evidence still returned
collectDependencyAdvisories: a cleanly-audited coordinate with no advisory match -> appears in queriedCoordinates only, absent from BOTH matches and unresolvedDependencies
collectDependencyAdvisories: a coordinate with a confirmed advisory -> appears in both queriedCoordinates and matches
collectDependencyAdvisories: a coordinate that could not be resolved/checked at all -> appears in both queriedCoordinates and unresolvedDependencies

testLevels.purpose: Prove lockfile export fidelity: exact-locked versions are preferred, and non-exportable entries are gapped rather than mis-exported.
subjects: a poetry.lock entry with a git/path/url source -> excluded from the generated requirements file, added to unresolvedDependencies with a non-standard-source note
a poetry.lock entry with a plain PyPI source and a simple marker -> exported as `name==version; marker`
a plain pip requirements.txt entry with an exact `==` pin -> treated as exact-locked evidence
a plain pip requirements.txt entry with a version range -> pip-audit still runs against it, but the coordinate is also recorded in unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain
a plain pip project with no requirements.txt at all -> perManagerMode 'unsupported', no fallback to the ambient environment

testLevels.purpose: Prove collectDependencyAdvisories' per-manager gap-reporting and configuredDestination recording, with a fake pkg_audit invocation.
subjects: collectDependencyAdvisories: pkg_audit spawnError for a manager -> recorded in unavailableSources
collectDependencyAdvisories: unparseable/malformed output -> recorded in unavailableSources
collectDependencyAdvisories: every attempted manager's perManagerMode entry carries a configuredDestination, including a manager with zero matches or a failed run
collectDependencyAdvisories: repoPath itself fails computeContentIdentity's precondition -> the error propagates rather than being swallowed into a per-manager gap
fixturesNeeded: a fake pkg_audit invocation standing in for the real pkgAuditTool.execute call
repoPath fixtures with varying manifest combinations, nested requirements references, and lockfile entries with non-PyPI sources

testLevels.purpose: Prove pkgAuditTool's new, additive requirementsPath input and the generated file's concurrency-safe lifecycle.
subjects: pkgAuditTool.execute: no requirementsPath provided -> argv is identical to today for every manager
pkgAuditTool.execute: requirementsPath provided -> argv includes `-r <requirementsPath>`
two concurrent collectDependencyAdvisories calls each get a distinct, non-colliding generated temp file
the generated file is removed after both a successful and a failed pkg_audit call

testLevels.purpose: Prove exact-locked targeting actually audits the repository's own locked dependencies rather than a stray or ambient alternative, against a real subprocess -- gated behind INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1.
subjects: collectDependencyAdvisories against a real poetry project: a deliberately vulnerable version pinned in poetry.lock is found, while a different, non-vulnerable version named in a stray requirements.txt beside it is NOT what gets reported
fixturesNeeded: a real poetry project fixture with a known-vulnerable locked version and a conflicting stray requirements.txt, run only under INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1

alternativesConsidered.name: Minimal additive pkg_audit env override + per-call ephemeral allowlisting proxy
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add one optional `env` field to pkgAuditTool's existing inputSchema (cwd is already there), forwarded to runShell's own per-call env option; s2's orchestration module starts a short-lived allowlisting proxy and per-manager scoped cwd/env for exactly the duration of one audit call.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add one optional `requirementsPath?: string` field to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema (purely additive -- omitted, every manager behaves exactly as today); auditArgv's pip/pipenv/poetry cases append `-r <requirementsPath>` only when it is provided. s2's own module: (1) computes contentIdentity over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE required-input closure (following nested -r/-c references; a go module's full source tree) before running any manager; (2) enumerates every manager in scope, regenerating a fresh requirementsPath from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock for pipenv/poetry (never a stray requirements.txt) or using plain pip's own requirements.txt directly, written to a per-call-unique temp file cleaned up in a finally block; (3) runs pkg_audit with the same host access the controller has; (4) records each manager's configuredDestination (honestly labeled as configured, never observed), persisted per manager even for a clean or failed run; (5) recomputes contentIdentity once more after the last manager completes and stamps contentStable; (6) maps pkg_audit's raw output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], and (7) wraps the result into both the thin EvidenceProviderOutput and the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (sc2, now additionally carrying contentStable and perManagerMode[].configuredDestination per HLD revision 6). Revision 4 closes the TOCTOU/incomplete-closure/unobservable-destination/unspecified-wiring gaps the revision-3 reviewer found, without reintroducing any sandboxing; the choice of a1 over a2/a3 stands unchanged. Revision 5 further corrects: computeContentIdentity is a simple, shared, non-manager-aware hash over exactly targets.entries (restoring the HLD's 'one shared identity' invariant -- a manager-aware expansion inside it at revision 4 would have made s2's own identity diverge from whatever s3 computes over the same targets); manager closure coverage is checked SEPARATELY via verifyManagerClosureCoverage without touching the hash; lockfile export now excludes non-PyPI-sourced or unfaithfully-representable entries as explicit gaps rather than mis-exporting them; plain pip's unpinned entries are flagged version-uncertain; and the queriedCoordinates/matches/unresolvedDependencies accounting is corrected to allow a clean, successfully-checked coordinate to appear in queriedCoordinates alone.
pros: Reuses pkg_audit directly -- the only code change is pointing pip-family managers at the repo's own requirements via -r, satisfying ac2's 'not a new fetcher' requirement
No proxy, isolation, or verification machinery to build or maintain -- the reviewer runs with the same host access as the controller, per the HLD's revision-5 policy
Full, accurate resolution (no --no-deps/--require-hashes restriction) is preferred over a restricted one now that sandboxing is explicitly out of scope
cons: s2's own reports of which destination each manager reached are self-reported by the native tool, not independently verified -- an accepted, documented tradeoff (HLD risky bit 'Controller-equivalent access tradeoff'), not a gap this Story tries to close

verifyManagerClosureCoverage adds one more per-manager check before any audit runs; a manager whose closure reaches outside targets.entries is refused even though a willing orchestrator could simply have included those files -- the burden is explicitly on the caller to scope targets.entries correctly, not on s2 to guess or expand it

alternativesConsidered.name: A wholly separate scoped-audit fetcher bypassing pkg_audit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build a new, standalone dependency-advisory fetcher that duplicates argv-building and subprocess invocation for each manager itself, instead of calling pkgAuditTool at all.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write a new module that re-implements per-manager argv construction (duplicating auditArgv's logic, which is module-private and not exported from pkg/index.ts) and calls runShell directly with full control over cwd/env/proxy from the start, never touching pkgAuditTool's existing execute() path.
pros: Total control over every invocation detail from the first line, no coordination with pkg_audit's existing input/output shape at all
cons: Directly violates ac2's explicit text: 'implemented as the EvidenceProvider registry's dependency-sbom category wired to the existing pkg_audit tool ..., not a new fetcher' -- this alternative IS a new fetcher
Duplicates per-manager argv logic (auditArgv) that already exists and is already correct, doubling the maintenance surface for npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/pipenv/poetry/go/cargo argument shapes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac2's explicit text outright by being exactly the 'new fetcher' the Story forbids, and duplicates auditArgv's already-correct per-manager logic -- rejected regardless of its other merits.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mutate the daemon's own process.env around the pkg_audit call
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Avoid changing pkg_audit's code at all by temporarily overwriting process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY (and restoring it afterward) for the duration of the call, since pkgAuditTool.execute defaults to process.env when no env override is passed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Before calling pkgAuditTool.execute, set process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY to the ephemeral proxy's address and the manager's scoped settings; restore the prior values in a finally block after the call returns.
pros: Zero changes to pkg_audit's own source at all
cons: process.env is GLOBAL to the daemon's Node process, which the daemon's own threaded/session architecture runs concurrent, unrelated shell-backed tool calls inside (per the project's daemon.threads design) -- a security review's proxy env could leak onto, or be clobbered by, a completely unrelated concurrent shell call in the same process, a correctness and isolation hazard a1's per-call options.env entirely avoids

A restore-in-finally still has a window where a concurrent call on another async task sees the mutated environment, since Node's single-threaded event loop interleaves awaits -- this is not a theoretical risk given the daemon already runs many concurrent tool calls per session
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Nominally keeps ac2's wiring intact (same pkgAuditTool.execute call site, no schema change) but the enforcement mechanism itself is unsafe under the daemon's own concurrent, threaded session model -- a global process.env mutation is not a boundary sc2's 'enforced, not merely observed' advisoryDestination can rely on. Moot at revision 3 since no env-based network enforcement of any kind is attempted anymore, but a1's per-call scoping remains the better code-change pattern regardless.
